title: PDO connection - DSN, exceptions, and charset
keywords: how to connect to a database
answer: Create one PDO object with a DSN naming the driver, host, and database. Set the error mode to exceptions so failures throw instead of failing silently, and use utf8mb4 so emoji and Hindi text store correctly. Keep credentials in environment variables, never in code. This example is syntax-checked only because it needs a MySQL server.
pitfall: The default PDO error mode is silent, so failed queries return false with no message. Always set ERRMODE_EXCEPTION when you create the connection.

title: PDO fetch modes - assoc, object, class, and column
answer: FETCH_ASSOC returns rows as arrays, FETCH_OBJ as objects, and FETCH_CLASS fills an object of your class. Set the default fetch mode once on the connection so every query behaves the same. This example is syntax-checked only because it needs a database.
pitfall: fetchAll on a huge table loads every row into memory at once. Loop with fetch in a while loop when a result can be large.

title: PDO insert, update, delete - lastInsertId and row counts
answer: Use execute with an array of values for insert, update, and delete. lastInsertId returns the new auto-increment ID, and rowCount tells how many rows an update or delete changed. Wrap related writes in a transaction so they succeed or fail together. This example is syntax-checked only because it needs a database.
pitfall: Forgetting commit leaves the transaction open and locks rows. Always commit on success and roll back in a catch block on failure.

title: Pagination with PDO - LIMIT, OFFSET, and total counts
answer: Pagination reads one page with LIMIT and OFFSET, and counts the total separately so the UI can show page numbers. Bind LIMIT and OFFSET as integers, because some drivers reject them as strings. This example is syntax-checked only because it needs a database.
pitfall: Deep OFFSET pages get slower as the offset grows, because the database still scans the skipped rows. For large tables, paginate by the last seen ID instead.

title: PDO prepared statements - named and positional placeholders
keywords: how to run a pdo query
answer: Prepare once, execute with values. Named placeholders like :email read clearly, positional placeholders use ? in order. fetch returns one row, fetchAll returns all rows, and fetchColumn returns one value. This example is syntax-checked only because it needs a database.
pitfall: Reusing a statement after fetchAll without re-executing returns no rows. Execute again with new values before fetching.

title: PDO transactions - begin, commit, and rollback
answer: A transaction groups several writes into one atomic unit: either all of them land, or none do. Start with beginTransaction, commit on success, and roll back when any step throws. Never leave a transaction open across user input or slow work. This example is syntax-checked only because it needs a database.
pitfall: Calling rollBack when no transaction is active throws an exception of its own. Guard it with inTransaction.
